question: Lever 1 was to port wazabi r125's PASTA_DEPS_BATCH. Is the dependency phase actually unparallelised here, and if not, how well does it scale?
answer: The port is unnecessary: our fork already generates dependencies concurrently across a chunk's records, one thread per record, `threads` at a time. What it does not do is scale — 1.82x on 8 threads with the production setting, so about 43% of the phase behaves as serial, and 78% with global_dependencies_opt off.

already_implemented.mechanism: the pipelined path assembles every piece of a chunk in order, then runs machine.generate_dependencies(once(record)) on one thread per record in groups of `threads`, and emits in execution order
already_implemented.equivalent_to: wazabi r125/r126 PASTA_DEPS_BATCH, at chunk granularity

host: Apple M2 Pro 10-core, 16 GB (the development Mac); CPU record generation only, no proving

measured_today.mode: --mode r5-cycles on the pinned mainnet ELF, global_dependencies_opt left at its default (off)

the_bigger_lever.finding: global_dependencies_opt is worth far more than any further parallelisation: with it off the dependency phase is 225.0 s at one thread, with it on 50.6 s — about 174 s of the producer's work removed outright.
the_bigger_lever.status: already true in both manifest arms, and r120 records that turning it off makes every shard fail shard_cryptographic_verification

what_would_go_further: the serial 43% is unattributed: Machine::generate_dependencies carries no tracing span, so lever 2's span timing cannot see inside it. Per-record and per-chip timing inside the phase is the next measurement, and it is a fork change with a free local loop.
limits: one observation per thread count today; the committed baseline has two per count
